extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to the NEH Public Scholars program (independent writers, researchers, scholars, journalists, and other writers proposing nonfiction books for general audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars program, including eligibility, proposal content, documentation, review, and award/period-of-performance rules for book-length nonfiction aimed at general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — independent scholars and journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: This program encourages applications from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists. All applicants must propose a significant book likely to appeal to general audiences and must present evidence of their qualifications, including previous publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chances are the same as other applicants. Be sure the project is a significant book aimed at general readers and document qualifications (e.g., prior publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility — enrolled graduate students
rubrics_metrics.description: Students enrolled in a degree program are not eligible to apply to the Public Scholars program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are currently enrolled in a degree program, do not apply to this program; consider other NEH opportunities when eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable projects — translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation projects are unallowable under the Public Scholars program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-scholar translation applications should go to NEH’s Fellowships program; translation projects by a team of two or more collaborators should go to the Scholarly Editions and Translations program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative project funding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may not be divided among collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking funding for a co-author, each person must submit a separate application specifying individual contribution. External reviewers evaluate each application on its own merits; see Notice of Funding Opportunity C.3 ('Collaborative projects') for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience suitability — general readership required
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports books conceived and written for a general audience; proposed books may make scholarly contributions but professional scholars should not be the primary audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books primarily addressed to scholars are not suitable; such applicants should apply to NEH Fellowships or Summer Stipends instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record requirement (if no prior book)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not previously published a book with a commercial or university press, you are eligible only if you have published at least three articles or essays in general-interest publications that reach a large national or international audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Notice of Funding Opportunity section C.1 ('Eligible applicants') for additional information on previous publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation revisions are ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to revise and publish a dissertation are not eligible for the Public Scholars program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applicants may apply to the NEH Fellowships program or Summer Stipends program instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social sciences projects — humanistic methods/content required
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects in social sciences may be eligible if they fall into 'those aspects of the social sciences which have humanistic content and employ humanistic methods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields such as anthropology, sociology, archaeology, linguistics, political science, economics, international relations, psychology, and geography may be eligible provided methods do not rely primarily on statistical or mathematical analysis. Contact NEH staff if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying to multiple NEH programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may apply for other NEH grants to support the same project; NEH encourages applying to all programs for which you are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Notice of Funding Opportunity section C.3 ('Other Eligibility Information') for guidance about multiple applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting multiple awards — overlap and fiscal-year limits
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases you may accept only one award. You may not hold two or more NEH individual awards with overlapping periods of performance or in support of the same tasks, and you may not accept or hold two NEH individual awards in the same fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered more than one award, review Notice C.3 for exceptions and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH staff assistance limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH staff will answer questions about preparing your proposal and about eligibility, but staff members are not able to comment on draft proposals for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact program staff at publicscholar@neh.gov for eligibility and procedural questions; do not expect detailed feedback on draft narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your title should be descriptive of the project, substantive, free of specialized language, easily understood by the general public, and not exceed 125 characters (including spaces and punctuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid main titles that require a clarifying subtitle. When possible include places and dates to indicate scope. If a person is mentioned include dates and a descriptor. Use informative, specific words rather than puzzling or intriguing phrasing. Omit technical terms and jargon. Examples provided: prefer 'A History of Counterfeiting in the U.S., 1776-1900' over 'Fakes and Fakers: A History of Counterfeiting...'; 'Faith and Belief among New York City Catholics, 1945-1970' over 'Faith and Belief in the Catholic Community'; avoid 'Chronotopes and Horologics' jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH may re-title funded projects
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH reserves the right to re-title funded projects that do not follow agency guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award recipients are permitted to use their preferred title for any award products despite NEH retitling for administrative/materials purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference — notification and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will notify you by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has arrived. After Grants.gov notifies you that NEH has received your application, you may check the status of letters by logging in to NEH's secure area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will not send requests for letters until approximately January 11; use the secure website to monitor arrival and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing or undelivered letter requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter writer has not received the request, it is usually due to a junk e-mail filter or an incorrect e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may resend the upload link by logging into NEH’s secure area. To correct an email address error, contact program staff at publicscholar@neh.gov. Provide accurate addresses because NEH uses exactly what you enter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing letter writers after the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to change a letter writer after the application deadline by contacting program staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting a replacement, indicate which letter writer you want to replace and provide contact information, including e-mail, for the new person; contact publicscholar@neh.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late letters of reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Late letters of reference are accepted and NEH will automatically add them to your file as soon as uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If external reviewers have already reviewed your application, they may not take late letters into account; plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing letters do not automatically disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: A missing letter of reference does not disqualify your application, but reviewers may find the application less persuasive if letters are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to secure letters on time to maximize persuasiveness to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-deadline updates to application prohibited (except letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the application deadline, you may not change your application or add material to your file apart from letters of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to submit additional materials after the deadline; only letters may be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and access to reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications receive peer review; details about NEH’s review process are available in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsuccessful, the notification will contain instructions for requesting reviewers' comments; these comments may help revise the application for resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of journalistic research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Research through interviews, firsthand conversation, and internet information-gathering are acceptable methods but may not by themselves be sufficient to gain a full picture and effectively present it to general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider additional methods such as consulting previous publications, archival research, or contacting humanities scholars. In the 'Significance and contribution' section, discuss how your project relates to previous work and how it makes a new contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable types of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is open to projects using many different types of sources, including documents, books, artifacts, literary/visual works, print or digital publications, interviews, observation including participant observation, surveys or questionnaires, and other fieldwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Sources and organization' section of the project narrative should discuss your sources and research materials, how you will use them, and how they support your treatment of the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation thoroughness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports nonfiction only. Your documentation of sources should make clear how you know what you are telling your reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For biographies, be careful to indicate when you are speculating about a subject's perceptions or thoughts and avoid introducing detail with no firm basis. NEH has a research misconduct policy addressing fabrication and plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of documentation — balance readability and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of documentation (footnotes, endnotes, etc.) is up to you and your publisher, but you should balance readability and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent footnotes may annoy general readers; endnotes keyed to phrases can be preferable if they do not create ambiguity about source attribution. If the writing sample is from the proposed book, it should demonstrate your documentation approach; if not, the 'Final product and dissemination' section should indicate how you'll handle documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation for professional scholars adapting work for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional scholars should keep in mind that Review Criterion 1 judges proposed books on appeal and intellectual significance for general readers; superficial changes to academic writing are usually insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than minimal adjustments (reducing notes, explaining terms), craft a project with an urgent motivation that matters to general readers. Use storytelling effectively, shorten chapters, limit examples, and return to the big picture regularly. Scholarly debates and names are often best relegated to notes and the bibliography. If the project is not well suited, consider Fellowships or Summer Stipends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable period of performance — part-time/full-time flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may be held part-time or combined part-time and full-time during the period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: working half-time for six months is equivalent to three full-time months; award dollar value would be adjusted accordingly (e.g., $5,000/month × equivalent full-time months). See Notice B.2 ('Summary of funding') for funding details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum period of performance is six full-time months (or the equivalent amount of part-time or combined full- and part-time work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants requesting a period shorter than six months are subject to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting work outside the period of performance disallowed
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not count work done before or after the stated period of performance toward the minimum requirement of six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed period of performance itself meets the minimum; do not attempt to include preparatory or follow-on work to meet the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of performance must be continuous. You must work at least half-time on your project throughout your period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working part time some months and full time other months is allowable and can still be continuous. A one-month reduction to half-time does not break continuity; the award amount would be reduced to reflect half-time status during that month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission confirmation responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the applicant's responsibility to confirm that Grants.gov and NEH have received the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Grants.gov 'Track my Application' tool and consult Notice D.4 ('Submission Dates and Times') to verify submission and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-U-N-S® and TIN/EIN requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a U.S. institutional affiliation must provide their institution's D-U-N-S® number on the NEH Supplemental Form for Individuals; TIN/EIN numbers are usually available from an institution's sponsored research office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D-U-N-S numbers are issued by Dun & Bradstreet and consist of nine digits. Use institutional resources or D&B advanced search to find these numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason for collecting institutional D-U-N-S® numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the program is for individual applicants, NEH requires a U.S. institution's D-U-N-S® number so that institutions' names are listed correctly in the NEH database and in materials provided to external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the accurate D-U-N-S number to ensure correct institutional identification in NEH systems and reviewer materials.
